newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- A Tweefontein Collieries mine manager was killed and a mine employee injured at the Waterpan colliery near Ogies in Mpumalanga on Wedensday when they were attacked by a mob of about 500 men believed to be Tweefontein workers.
- The African National Congress (ANC) on Wednesday accused policemen of carrying out the execution style killing of five party members - including two newly elected councillors - in Richmond.

- Avgold managed Hartebeestfontein HBFL.PA was "far down the line" towards reaching agreement with labour on new work schedules aimed at improving the operation's precarious financial position, sources said on Wednesday.

- Investment holding company Hunt Leuchars & Hepburn Holdings (HL&H) said on Wednesday its loss for the six months to September would be "significantly higher than had been expected", due largely to "severe pressure" on South Africa's broiler chicken industry.

- Preparations for next week's meeting of the U.S.-South Africa Binational Commission hit a rough spot when the U.S. side was told that Defence Minister Joe Modise was refusing to set foot in the Pentagon because of U.S. policy on Cuba and other issues.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The Post Office, which received a 572 million rand state subsidy in the 1995-96 financial year, has been given five years to get back into the black, sources said on Wednesday.
- The Community Growth Fund's (CGF) blacklist of companies that do not meet its investment criteria has risen to 18. It includes Anglo American, Iscor, Minorco, Rembrandt and Reunert.
- Sentiment on the bond market firmed on Wednesday, with long-dated gilts breaking through technical levels, dealers said.
- State warehouses in Durban were so crammed with seized goods that private companies had been asked to provide warehousing space, industry sources said on Wednesday.
- Monterey, the landmark Cape Town head-quarters of the Seardel group for the past 15 years, is being put on the market with a price tag of 15 million rand.
SAKE BEELD
- Stock exchanges worldwide, including the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, on Wednesday closed higher after sharp gains on Wall Street overnight.
- JCI and Absa are the latest companies to be approved for investment by the Community Growth Fund.
- Plessey South Africa is going to get a piece of Telkom's two billion rand contract to install 420,000 new phone lines over the next two years using cordless digital technology.
THE STAR
- The powder keg that is Richmond exploded late on Tuesday night when five ANC members - including two councillors - were assassinated in cold blood in the remote Isimozimeni area.

- The National Conventional Arms Control Committee has issued arms producer Denel with a contracting application for the sale of G-6 artillery pieces to a country in the Middle East, NCACC chairman Kader Asmal said on Wednesday.

- The classroom is not a catwalk to sport the latest fashions. This is what pupils of the Rustenburg High school in North West found out this week when they were given the marching orders for not being properly dressed.
- Police said on Wednesday the fraud investigation involving Parliament's Deputy Speaker, Baleka Mbete-Mgositsile, had been transferred to the fraud unit in Cape Town.
